chunks: And from him, from al-Nakha'i, from Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"It is not fitting for the people of Mecca to wear the qamis (long shirt) and to resemble the pilgrims in ihrām with disheveled hair and dusty appearance."
And he said: "The ruler should enforce this upon them."

key_terms.الْقَمِيص: A long shirt or tunic, a specific garment worn in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabia.
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِينَ: Those in the state of ihrām, the sacred ritual status for Hajj or 'Umrah.
key_terms.شُعْثاً غُبْراً: Disheveled hair and dusty/dirty appearance, characteristic of the state of ihrām.

ai.seo_question: Why should the people of Mecca avoid wearing the qamis and resembling pilgrims?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs the residents of Mecca to avoid wearing the qamis and appearing disheveled, ensuring they do not visually mimic pilgrims in the state of ihrām, thereby preserving the distinct sanctity of the ritual. This ruling highlights the scholarly emphasis on external signs of piety and the ruler's (al-Sultan) role in enforcing these social distinctions to maintain the spiritual integrity of the pilgrimage season.
